summary: 1933 Aermotor LS-40 steel tower built by Whitney Park; privately owned, reopened as a 1.2-mile hike on September 2, 2023 after a Long Lake and Hamilton County restoration.

access.note: Opened to the public on September 2, 2023 by the Town of Long Lake with Hamilton County. Reached on a 1.2-mile one-way trail with 500 feet of elevation gain from a trailhead lot on South Sabattis Road. The land belongs to Cedar Heights Timber LLC, which granted a trail easement. The town's notice does not say whether visitors may enter the cab.

visit.trail_note: 1.2 miles one way, 500 feet of elevation gain, from the trailhead parking lot on South Sabattis Road off NYS Route 30

facts.agency: Private owner Cedar Heights Timber LLC; trail and reopening led by the Town of Long Lake with Hamilton County

events.note: Whitney Park erected the 60-foot Aermotor LS-40 steel tower to protect its lands; tower parts were hauled up by sled dogs in winter; a wooden fire observatory may have stood on the summit before it
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on December 25, 2022; the register page then anticipated a summer 2022 reopening
Register anticipated a summer 2022 reopening under an agreement between the owner and Hamilton County; the tower did not open until September 2023
Final phase of the trail and tower project: tower rehabilitation with a new sheet metal roof, treads, galvanized steps and fencing. The town's notice does not date this work
Tower opened to the public on September 2, 2023 after a 1.2-mile trail was built over two summer seasons by Adirondack Mountain Club crews and partners

corrections.current: Town of Long Lake and partners installed all-new stairs, landings and roof by August; FFLA volunteers and town staff then painted the tower (2022)
corrections.proposed: Rehabilitation (new sheet metal roof, treads, galvanized steps, fencing) was the final phase of the trail and tower project that opened September 2, 2023; the notice does not date it to 2022. Painting by FFLA volunteers not confirmed.
corrections.why: The town's notice dates the opening to September 2, 2023 and calls the rehabilitation the project's final phase with no 2022 date. The August 2022 date and the FFLA painting were not found in any page read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register page (registered December 2022) anticipated a summer 2022 reopening. The September 2023 newsletter and the town's notice record the opening on September 2, 2023, so the later record is used.
The register gives 2,425 ft (739 m); the town notice gives the summit as 2400 feet. Both are reported as stated, and the story gives each with its own source.
The town's notice says a wooden fire observatory may have stood on the summit before the steel tower. The register does not mention one. Kept as the town's belief, not stated as fact.

notes_for_editor: Core facts (1933 build, private owner Cedar Heights Timber LLC, September 2, 2023 opening, trail details) are confirmed by two or three sources each. Not confirmed: the brief's 2022 restoration details (stairs, roof, painting by August 2022), which the town notice does not support; a correction is proposed above. The brief's Sept 15, 2023 ribbon cutting appears in the town notice as scheduled, not as held, so it is not in the story. The brief's height was absent; 60 ft converted to 18.3 m. Whether climbing the cab is permitted is not stated in any source. The NHLR page is stale on the reopening date. A HistoriCorps caption that appeared only as a search snippet (not opened, not cited) gives a 1939 build date, which conflicts with the 1933 date in the register and the newsletter; the editor may want to check it. The Adirondack Almanack and Wikipedia results were seen only as search snippets and are not cited.
